text:
Just saw a LinkedIn Influencer with 'Organic Growth' written in the profile with 65K+ followers sharing a sponsored course on how to grow without paid ads. 
Irony just left the chat.

Jobseekers, this one's for you.
 Every application, every interview, every follow-up... the pressure is real. 
Take a breath. Your worth is not defined by a rejection email.
Looking for jobs on LinkedIn is like online dating: Full of promises, but in the end, you're just left ghosted.

LinkedIn scams be like: 'Congratulations, you've been selected for an interview for a role you never applied to!' 

Block, report, move on.

Every time I poured my heart into 5-6 rounds of interviews and faced rejection, it felt like a punch in the gut. But looking back, every single 'no' redirected me to the place where I was truly valued.

To everyone who's still looking for a job...

I see you. I feel you. 

Every rejection email hurts, every ghosted interview stings. But don't let silence from recruiters define your self-worth. Keep showing up.
Sometimes, we forget that a company's brand name doesn't define someone's talent. It's easy to judge someone from a lesser-known startup, but grit and skill speak louder than any pedigree.
So when I left a toxic work environment, I told my manager a simple truth: No title or paycheck is worth losing my mental peace and sanity.

sapne dekhna achi baat hai,
lekin job ka sapna dekh ke 'interested' comment karte rehna bekar baat hai.
Take action, upskill, and reach out directly.
Next time when I'll be reading some LinkedIn Influencer's story, I am definitely checking if common sense was harmed in the process.

Cold emailing works, but sending 'Dear Sir, please find attached my CV' to 50 HRs without context doesn't. Personalize your outreach, mention how you can solve their problem, and see the response rate change.
A quick reminder for mid-week: You don't have to hustle 24/7 to prove you are ambitious. Rest is part of the work.
